rule.name: Persist Claude conversation events to the local spool
rule.description: Every UserPromptSubmit and Stop hook event MUST write its raw payload to the local spool, from which a drain ships it to MongoDB. The hook does no network I/O: it copies bytes to disk and exits, so no remote outage can slow or fail an utterance. The spool is the queue -- durable, with an explicit ack (the file is deleted only after MongoDB confirms the write). Kafka and the HTTP producer sidecar were removed on 2026-08-07: they were two additional components that could be down, and both were, while adding nothing the local filesystem does not already provide for a single workstation. This rule implements the capture leg of EPIC-008-F-013-S-001.

rule_statement.statement_body: On every UserPromptSubmit hook event, the raw hook payload MUST be written to the spool at C:	mp\ChatHealthySpool as write-<guid>-<time_ns>.txt and then renamed in place to read-<guid>-<time_ns>.txt. The rename is what makes the file visible only once complete. The payload MUST NOT be parsed, and the writer MUST NOT open a network connection.
On every Stop hook event, the raw hook payload MUST be written to the spool by the same mechanism as statement 1.

If the spool cannot be written, a browser MUST be invoked and a viewport-filling page displayed telling the operator the utterance was NOT recorded. Failure to write the spool is the only condition under which an utterance is lost.

enforcement.title: Persist every operator utterance to the local spool
Persist every Claude response to the local spool

rule.name: Boot execution on SessionStart and PostCompact
rule.description: Wires the ChatHealthy boot program into the V19 engineering-rules architecture. The boot executable runs on SessionStart and PostCompact: SessionStart fires for new sessions and new logins; PostCompact fires when Claude Code auto-compacts its context. Both events trigger the same boot duties so Claude resumes with fresh conversation context and the business taxonomy regardless of how the session was disrupted. The boot reads the hook payload from stdin and dispatches on hook_event_name. Replaces the legacy direct settings.json wiring of chathealthy_devops_boot.py with rule-dispatched invocation through chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py.

rule_statement.statement_body: On SessionStart and PostCompact, the boot MUST read the 170 most recent utterance documents from MongoDB ClaudeCodeUtterances.utterances, trim each document to {actor, content}, order newest-to-oldest, and emit them as part of the hook's additionalContext so Claude resumes with recent conversation context. If the MongoDB read fails, the boot MUST fail open — log the failure and continue with remaining duties.

On SessionStart and PostCompact, the boot MUST read brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json and emit the business taxonomy as part of the hook's additionalContext: every epic's id, name, and description; every feature's id, name, and description; every story's id and name. Story descriptions, requirements, and tests MUST NOT be emitted.

The boot MUST read the Claude Code hook payload JSON from stdin and dispatch on the hook_event_name field. SessionStart and PostCompact MUST each execute the duties in statements 1 and 2. Any other hook_event_name value MUST be a no-op that exits 0.

chathealthy_devops_boot.py MUST NOT appear directly in .claude/settings.json hooks. It is invoked exclusively via Rule-002 enforcement entries dispatched by chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py. .claude/settings.json registers only the enforcement manager (one entry per hook); the manager loads engineering_rules.json and spawns the matching enforcement workers.

On SessionStart and PostCompact, the boot MUST compare the current line count of %TEMP%/chathealthy_consumer_errors.log to a line-count semaphore at %TEMP%/chathealthy_last_boot_error_line.txt. If the current line count exceeds the semaphore, the boot MUST emit one line to additionalContext naming the file path and the new line range. The boot MUST then update the semaphore to the current line count. If the error file does not exist, the boot MUST treat the line count as 0 and emit nothing.

enforcement.title: Boot the session again after a context compaction

rule.name: Constrain Claude Code's use of tools via the Anthropic preTool hook
rule.description:
Unimplemented, undesigned and inappropriately specified. This rule carries no enforcement and no implementing code; the worker that realized it (llm_classify_shell_invocation_worker.py) and its operator wrapper (oneoff.py) have been deleted. Rule-064, which separately constrained tool calls through the same PreToolUse hook by blocking paths under the legacy project tree, was deleted on 2026-08-10 together with its worker (block_legacy_path_worker.py); the two rules covered one concern and neither had constrained a tool call since 2026-08-04.

What must be done is not stated here. It is specified by story EPIC-008-F-002-S-013 under feature EPIC-008-F-002, requirements EPIC-008-F-002-S-013-REQ-B-001 through EPIC-008-F-002-S-013-REQ-B-012. That story is the sole statement of requirement for this rule.

The eight rule_statements below are retained as the record of the withdrawn five-stage-funnel design. They are NOT requirements and they are not in force. BUG-002 records why the design failed.

rule_statement.statement_body: Stage 1 - local allowlist. PreToolUse MUST match the tool_input.command text against a hardcoded allowlist of shell verbs whose effect is structurally confined to the local filesystem (this workstation, git tree, tmp dirs). The allowlist also includes `git push` in any non-force form (excluding --force, -f, --force-with-lease, --force-if-includes, and delete-remote-ref syntax `origin :branch`) because Rule-065 statement 1 makes push-after-authorized-commit implicit in the commit authorization - the commit has already cleared the pre-commit gate, so the accompanying push carries no additional governance need. If every shell-separator-delimited segment of the command matches the allowlist, classify as allow and exit 0 silently WITHOUT invoking the LLM. Script invocations (python foo.py, pytest, bash foo.sh, powershell foo.ps1, npm run, poetry run) are NEVER allowlisted regardless of the script's contents - those always proceed to Stage 2. Network verbs (curl, wget, ftp, ssh) are NEVER allowlisted. Force-push variants of git push are NEVER allowlisted; those are destructive and require explicit operator approval via the oneoff.py wrapper.

Stage 2 - recursive code-path walk. For any command not matched by Stage 1, PreToolUse MUST perform a bounded transitive walk of every project script the command references: Python files parsed with ast.parse and followed via import/subprocess.run/call/Popen/check_output/os.system/os.popen/runpy/importlib.import_module; shell/ps1 files scanned for source/dot-source/backtick/$(...) invocations. Only project-local files (under the git repo root, not stdlib or third-party wheels) are followed. Walker MUST cap at 60 nodes and 6 levels of depth; cycles broken via visited-set. Any file referenced but not resolvable inside the project tree, or any dynamic-code pattern (exec/eval/compile of a runtime string, subprocess.run with a runtime-constructed arg, importlib on a computed name) MUST be surfaced to the LLM as a walk_error or dynamic_evidence entry so the classifier can factor the uncertainty.

Stage 3 - LLM classification. PreToolUse MUST submit the payload (tool_name + command + wrapper info + all walked files with sha256 fingerprints + walk_errors + dynamic_evidence) to Google model gemini-2.5-flash-lite via the generativelanguage.googleapis.com endpoint. Per-attempt timeout MUST be 75 seconds wall clock; up to 6 attempts on 429/5xx and network errors with exponential backoff starting at 2 seconds (doubling) plus random jitter to avoid thundering-herd retries. Deterministic 4xx errors other than 429 (400/401/403/404/etc.) MUST NOT retry - those are surfaced immediately with the specific HTTP code embedded in the reason. API key MUST be loaded from Code/.env (GEMINI_API_KEY, falling back to GOOGLE_API_KEY). Classifier output MUST be strict JSON with exactly two fields: classification (allow | gate_approve | reject) and reason (<=70-word plain-English explanation naming the remote resource, the offending line if applicable, and the rationale). On LLM error/timeout after retries, on missing API key, on unparsable response, or on any other classifier-side failure, classification MUST default to gate_approve (NOT reject) - the operator is prompted for approval so a transient Gemini outage never silently blocks legitimate work. The gate_approve prompt reason MUST include the actual LLM failure text so the operator can distinguish transient outages from deterministic misconfiguration. Verdicts produced from an LLM error path MUST NOT be cached.

Stage 4 - outcome dispatch. On allow, exit 0 silently and the tool call proceeds. On gate_approve, prompt the operator via inline APPROVE echo in a real interactive TTY, or via a local browser page opened by the worker in agent contexts (the popup displays the exact command, the classifier's <=70-word reason, and Claude's wrapper explanation if present); on operator APPROVE the tool call proceeds; on REJECT or timeout, deny with a fire-and-forget browser notification. On reject, deny IMMEDIATELY with a fire-and-forget browser notification - no operator prompt. Verdicts MUST be cached by payload-hash (SHA256 of command + walked file hashes + wrapper explanation) so identical commands do not re-hit the LLM; cached verdicts still trigger the same operator prompt (gate_approve) or notification (reject).

Stage 5 - oneoff wrapper. Claude's legal path to run a command that mutates REMOTE state is by wrapping it: `python architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/oneoff.py --explanation "<claude's plain-English description in 4-70 words>" -- <inner command...>`. Two Stage-1 accommodations bypass the wrapper: (a) the ChatHealthy canonical build/deploy/promote chain surfaces (build_chathealthy.py, deploy_chathealthy.py, promote_chathealthy.py) which are allowlisted at Stage 1 per operator direction 2026-07-23 - firing those scripts is itself the operator's authorization since they encode the sanctioned deployment process, so no per-invocation popup fires; (b) `git push` (non-force forms) whose authorization is implicit in the commit that Rule-065 already gated. All other remote-mutating commands (bare `az`, direct `docker push`, `wrangler`, `gh api` writes, `curl -X POST/PUT/DELETE`, etc.) require the oneoff wrapper. The classifier detects the wrapper at the top-level command surface, extracts Claude's explanation, reads the inner command AND every script the walker reaches transitively, and MUST verify the explanation truthfully describes what the inner command actually does. Honest match => classification gate_approve. Explanation missing, dishonest, evasive, or omitting a remote-state effect => classification reject. Unwrapped remote-mutating commands outside the two Stage-1 accommodations => classification reject with a notification that Claude did not use the wrapper.

Categorical rules baked into the classifier's system prompt: (a) Local filesystem work is ALWAYS allow regardless of file name or contents - editing a manifest is NOT deploying it, editing engineering_rules.json is NOT enforcing it, editing Code/.env is NOT publishing secrets. (b) No chain-surface auto-allow. deploy_chathealthy.py, build_chathealthy.py, promote_chathealthy.py, and every other program are walked like any other command; if they mutate remote state they require the wrapper (or a per-script in-line operator APPROVE prompt) same as anything else. (c) Reaches remote means: Azure/Cloudflare/MongoDB Atlas/Hugging Face/Azure Container Registry/GitHub-remote/pypi.org write-mode/npm.js write-mode; any HTTP POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH to an external host; any az/aws/gcloud/atlas/gh/wrangler/docker push invocation contacting remote APIs. (d) curl/wget GET requests to public read-only endpoints are allow; POST/PUT/DELETE or auth-carrying calls are gate_approve (if wrapped) or reject. (e) Reading harness temp files (paths under /tmp, C:/Users/*/AppData/Local/Temp/, task-output area) is ALWAYS allow.

Every remote-mutation attempt MUST fire a browser notification to the operator: interactive popup on gate_approve (operator acts before the command runs), passive fire-and-forget popup on reject (operator is informed after the deny). Notifications MUST include the tool name, the exact command, the code fingerprints (sha256[:16]) of every walked file, the classifier's <=70-word reason, and - on reject when the command was unwrapped - a note explaining that Claude did not use the oneoff.py wrapper and must do so if the intent is legitimate. Every classification (allow, gate_approve with approve/reject outcome, reject) MUST be recorded to the audit log at architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/ArchitectureDesignAndAuditDocs/llm_classify_shell_invocation.log.

Deploy-from-git preflight (runs before Stage 1). Any invocation of deploy_chathealthy.py or promote_chathealthy.py with --env dev|qa|prod MUST be denied unless the working tree is clean AND HEAD is at origin/<current-branch>. Local-env deploys (--env local) are exempt. This check runs before classification because the LLM cannot see git state. Denial fires the same reject notification as classification reject.

rule.name: No commit without explicit human authorization
rule.description:
Every commit is explicitly authorized by the operator at the moment it fires, and no commit enters the repository ungoverned. Both halves are this one rule: the authorization prompt and every check that gates a commit are enforcements of it.

The checks previously stood as separate rules -- Rule-003, Rule-004, Rule-005, Rule-007, Rule-008, Rule-009 and Rule-066 -- each holding one pre-commit enforcement. That split a single concern across seven artifacts which then drifted apart from one another. They were folded in on 2026-08-10; their statements are below, each prefixed with the rule id it came from.

A real interactive terminal satisfies the authorization with an exact-match APPROVE token typed at a prompt naming the action; every other context is served a local browser page with APPROVE and REJECT, blocking until the operator clicks or the 600-second timeout rejects. The `git push` that immediately follows is the network operation completing the commit and needs no separate authorization.

rule_statement.statement_body: No commit takes place without explicit human authorization given at the moment it fires. Commits land on the dev branch and no other; qa and prod receive code only through promote. The push that completes a commit is implicit in that authorization and needs no separate one.

Every deliberate raise authored in ChatHealthy.ai code uses ChatHealthyException with a mode discriminator. The class is required rather than a list of built-ins forbidden: a raise that constructs anything else is a violation. A bare re-raise is always allowed, and so is re-raising a bound name, since neither authors an exception. One further raise is allowed and no others: inside a function registered as a pydantic-ai output validator, a raise of ModelRetry. That is not an authored exception but the library's callback protocol -- our function is called by pydantic-ai, which catches ModelRetry in its own frame to ask the model again, and there is no other way to reject an answer. The object never enters ChatHealthy code and no catch site of ours ever sees it. Both halves are required: the function MUST carry the output_validator decorator, and the class raised MUST be ModelRetry. The decorator is what proves the place, not the function's name, because the decorator is the registration. Such a function MAY log before it raises, and is not required to: a thrower stays silent elsewhere because the catcher logs, and here the catcher is the library and will never log to ours, so that prohibition does not reach this case and the author decides. A catch that binds the caught exception and converts it to ChatHealthyException carries the original in exception=; an external exception keeps its native type until a boundary converts it, and a conversion that drops the original leaves the mode saying what kind of failure occurred and nothing saying what failed. Exception management is one concern and one enforcement carries it.

A MongoDB handle is obtained only through ChatHealthyMongoUtilities().getConnection(identity, cluster). The rule binds at acquisition: constructing a client, taking one from a static -- an imported module or a class defined in the same file -- or standing any fake, mock, stub or in-memory double in place of a client, database or collection. An attribute off self, off cls or off a local is ordinary code and is not acquisition. A component handed a handle by its caller is using one another component authenticated for, so passing a handle on is allowed. A connection-string literal is forbidden wherever it appears. There is no test-file exemption: the certificate is the credential, and code that reaches Mongo without an identity is code whose authorization is never tested.

Logging goes through ChatHealthyLoggingService. Outside the service itself, the stdlib logging module is not imported and print() is not used; an exc= argument is a ChatHealthyException; and a function that raises does not also log, because the catcher logs, not the thrower.

A commit that changes identity or role grants in deployment_architecture.json -- the IdentityCatalog, the CustomRoleCatalog, or any target's allowed_roles -- requires explicit operator approval. A commit that touches none of those surfaces proceeds without one.

Every file committed is architecturally compliant: brain JSON validates against the schema its $schema names, no file carries an insecure http:// URL outside the allowed set, executable front-end and pipeline code contains no regular expressions, and no build-package file carries a value held in the local secret store.

Display, plumbing and logic stay separate. React owns display authoring. The one exception is a static page: a file that deployment_architecture.json assigns to the static_pages package is a page, and a page authors its own display. Every other authored .js and .html authors no display content, including the wrapper's own runtime driver. Authored .js and .html carry no business logic wherever they live, and the React application changes no persistent state directly, every change originating from a /gate call dispatched through ClientRouter.

The build, deploy and promote chain has exactly three operator-facing entry points -- build_chathealthy.py, deploy_chathealthy.py and promote_chathealthy.py. Every other top-level file in that directory is an imported-only helper and carries no entry-point block.

The one file that migrates data to the front-end serving database satisfies every requirement of story EPIC-010-F-108-S-001. The requirements are read from the backlog and each is put to an LLM against the file's source; a requirement the code does not enforce, or that could not be established, stops the commit. No other file writes to that database.

enforcement.title: No commit without explicit human authorization
A MongoDB handle is acquired only through the canonical utility
Identity and role-grant changes require operator approval
Every committed file is architecturally compliant
Display, plumbing and logic stay separate
Exactly three build, deploy and promote entry points
The data migration satisfies every requirement of its story
